newsitem.title: UK: Oman debut bond issue twice oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Oman debut bond issue twice oversubscribed.

text.p: Oman on Monday issued its first international bond issue and the sought-after $225 million deal was twice oversubscribed.
"The deal has gone extremely well," an official at underwriter J.P. Morgan said.

"We were twice oversubscribed at launch even after the issue size was increased from an expected $150 million. The $225 million was the largest size the borrower wanted to issue, because we could easily have sold a larger deal," he said.
The small oil-producing Gulf Arab state has investment grade ratings from two major rating agencies, Baa2 from Moody's Investors Service and BBB-minus and from Standard & Poor's.
These ratings are similar to Croatia's Baa3 and BBB-minus ratings, yet Oman's deal was priced more expensively than Croatia's recent $300 million five-year debut Eurobond.
Oman offered a 73 basis point spread over U.S. Treasury notes. Croatia's bond was priced at an 80 b.p. spread.

"The pricing reminds one of the unique nature of the credit. There has been a volatile U.S. Treasury and emerging market environment, but Oman had a strong story as the first investment grade Arab borrower," the J.P. Morgan official said.

"We lost one order amongst all the turbulence from a U.S. account last Friday. Other investors heard the story, read the research and recognised the unique strengths of the country and wanted to participate in the bond," he said.
After an almost uninterruped surge in emerging market debt prices for more than a year, spreads jumped last week on increased expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
Oman's bond followed a series of investor presentations in Europe and the U.S. by senior government officials.
During such a meeting in London in February, Oman's Minister of State for Development Affairs Mohamed Musa al-Yousef said the aim of the bond was to "put Oman on the map for international investors".

"The most important things we want is to diversify our sources of funding and acquaint investors with Oman, not just for borrowing but also for investment. We are inviting a lot of foreign direct investment at the moment," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
